sections.answer: Guidelines on fulfilling due diligence obligations, guidance on the fitness of industry or multi-stakeholder initiatives
sections.components:
- c1: Guidelines on fulfilling due diligence obligations
- c2: guidance on the fitness of industry or multi-stakeholder initiatives
sections.evidence:
- D02 (Article 19(1), L677) [c1]: "shall issue guidelines, including general guidelines and sector-specific guidelines or guidelines for specific adverse impacts"
- D01 (Article 13, L835) [c1]: "may issue guidelines, including for specific sectors or specific adverse impacts"
- D02 (Article 20(4), L719) [c2]: "The Commission, in collaboration with Member States, shall issue guidance setting out fitness criteria and a methodology for companies to assess the fitness of industry and multi-stakeholder initiatives."
- D01 (Article 14(4), L847) [c2]: "The Commission, in collaboration with Member States, may issue guidance for assessing the fitness of industry schemes and multi-stakeholder initiatives."
- D02 (Article 20(5), L723) [c2]: "shall issue guidance setting out fitness criteria and a methodology for companies to assess the fitness of third-party verifiers"
- D02 (Article 18, L671) [c1]: "shall adopt guidance about voluntary model contractual clauses"
- D01 (Article 12, L829) [c1]: "the Commission shall adopt guidance about voluntary model contract clauses"
sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: h1 (notes/hooks.md), permission in the proposal against duty in the adopted text, asked from the adopted side over the Commission's guidance. Target medium (user, 2026-10-13: no Easy slot, "target medium and high"). Measured platform result pending; no earlier capture on these bytes.
- Dependency plan: D02 gives the guidance duties: Article 18 L671 (model clauses), Article 19(1) L677 (guidelines), Article 20(4) L719 (fitness of industry and multi-stakeholder initiatives), Article 20(5) L723 (fitness of third-party verifiers, with guidance on monitoring that verification). D01 gives the status of each in the proposal: Article 12 L829 "shall adopt guidance" (duty), Article 13 L835 "may issue guidelines" (permission), Article 14(4) L847 "may issue guidance for assessing the fitness" (permission), nothing on verifiers ("verifier" occurs nowhere in D01). Permission then duty: guidelines, and fitness guidance for initiatives.
- Universe: every sentence in the articles (D01 L527-L1085, D02 L229-L1063) with the Commission as actor and "may", "shall" or "empowered" was listed by script on 2026-10-13. Guidance or guidelines in D02's articles: Articles 18, 19(1)-(4), 20(4), 20(5); the contents listed in Article 19(2)(a)-(g) are parts of the Article 19 guidelines, not separate instruments. In D01's articles: Articles 12, 13, 14(4). D02 Article 21's helpdesk lets companies "seek information, guidance and support"; it is a helpdesk, not guidance the Commission issues, and D01 has no helpdesk.
- Necessity: D01 is the only source of what the proposal's articles allowed or required (D02 and D03 do not describe the proposal's wording; D03 L49 mentions "non-binding guidelines" as a stakeholder view). Without D01 neither component can be told apart from the two decoys. D02 is the only source of the adopted duties. Without D02 it is unknown which permissions became duties: D01 Article 14(3) and the first sentence of 14(4) hold permissions that stayed permissions (D02 Article 20(3), 20(4) first sentence).
- Selected-lever checks: which-items decoys that fail the test. Model contractual clauses guidance: required by D02 Article 18 but already "shall" in D01 Article 12 (the memorandum's L179 "Guidelines may also be used to outline non-binding model contractual clauses" is not an article, and the memorandum's own article summary at L317 calls Article 12 an "obligation"). Third-party verifier guidance: required by D02 Article 20(5), absent from D01. Careless results: every guidance duty of D02 (the two gold items plus verifiers and model clauses, four items); the twin fitness sentences taken together (three items); only the headline change, the guidelines (one item). Recitals checked for the same points on 2026-10-13: D01 recitals (37), (45), (46) and D02's guidance recitals use the same verbs as their articles ("may" or "should have the possibility" against "should issue").
- Targeted failure modes: Linking across documents / Wrong members in a list: D02 Article 20(4) and 20(5) are twin sentences; only the first has a counterpart in D01 Article 14(4). Wrong lists recomputed above (four, three or one item). Not declared: a reading from the memorandum that treats model clauses as optional in the proposal (the question says "articles"); unobserved so far. To be matched to the observed wrong answers after the first run, before Submit.
- Calculation verification: not applicable (no arithmetic, no dates).
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: the bundle overview names neither item. Searching "may issue" in D01 lands on Article 13 and Article 14(4) (and recital 37, memorandum L179 and L321); searching "shall issue" in D02 lands on Articles 19(1), 20(4) and 20(5). No passage in either document states which permissions became duties. Shortest route: the three guidance articles in each text, compared verb by verb.
- Precision/readings: (1) verifier guidance read as "allowed" because the proposal did not forbid it: the question says the proposal's articles "had merely allowed it", and they do not mention it. (2) Model clauses read as optional from the memorandum: rejected by "the articles". (3) The guidelines answered at the level of Article 19(2)'s contents (sector-specific guidance, guidance on specific adverse impacts): the same instrument, component c1. (4) The helpdesk read as guidance: Article 21 sets up a helpdesk; it issues nothing named guidance. Readings (1) to (3) stay possible on a quick read; the form's "One defensible answer" check and the run will show whether solvers take them.
- Completeness: complete capture, no gaps (notes/intake.json). Articles of both texts read in full for this question (D02 Articles 10-13 scanned by script for the Commission's "may" and "shall" sentences: none on guidance).
- Style/set review: 34 words, one ask, list of two items with the order left free. q01 (statement timing, 38 months) and the spares i06, i07 and i02 share no answer path with it. Author run 2 looked at this hook in its broad form ("tasks") and did not promote it: "task" was open (helpdesk, verifier guidance) and the memorandum is loose on model clauses. This write-up narrows the ask to guidance and to the proposal's articles for those two reasons.
- Warnings answered: see the floor output recorded at hand-over.

sections.question: Which guidance, if any, does the adopted due diligence directive require the Commission to issue where the articles of the Commission's original proposal had merely allowed it to? List the items in any order.
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 3, article headed "Guidelines"): to support companies and Member State authorities on how companies should fulfil their due diligence obligations, the Commission "shall issue guidelines". This is a duty.
Step 2. Source input (Doc 3, article headed "Accompanying measures"): the Commission "shall issue guidance setting out fitness criteria and a methodology for companies to assess the fitness of industry and multi-stakeholder initiatives". The next paragraph requires the same for "the fitness of third-party verifiers", with guidance on monitoring their verification. All of these are duties.
Step 3. Source input (Doc 3, article headed "Model contractual clauses"): the Commission "shall adopt guidance about voluntary model contractual clauses". Also a duty. Steps 1 to 3 are all the guidance the adopted directive's articles require the Commission to issue.
Step 4. Source input (Doc 1, article headed "Guidelines"): in the proposal the Commission "may issue guidelines, including for specific sectors or specific adverse impacts". That was a permission, so the guidelines qualify (first component).
Step 5. Source input (Doc 1, article headed "Accompanying measures"): the Commission "may issue guidance for assessing the fitness of industry schemes and multi-stakeholder initiatives". That was a permission too, so this guidance qualifies (second component). The proposal's articles say nothing about guidance on third-party verifiers, so that guidance was not something the proposal had allowed and it does not qualify.
Step 6. Source input (Doc 1, article headed "Model contractual clauses"): the proposal already said the Commission "shall adopt guidance about voluntary model contract clauses". It was a duty from the start, so it does not qualify.
Decoy: the guidance on third-party verifiers sits in a sentence that mirrors the one on industry and multi-stakeholder initiatives, but the proposal has no such sentence. The guidance on model contractual clauses is required in both texts.
Step 7. Final answer (Doc 1 and Doc 3): two items moved from a permission in the proposal's articles to a duty in the adopted directive: the guidelines on fulfilling due diligence obligations, and the guidance on the fitness of industry or multi-stakeholder initiatives.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Linking across documents
How a careless solver fails: Wrong members in a list

Why these are traps: Linking across documents: Doc 3's Accompanying measures article requires fitness guidance twice, for initiatives and for third-party verifiers; Doc 1 allows only the first. Listing Doc 3's guidance duties unchecked adds verifiers and model clauses, four items. Matching each to Doc 1's wording leaves the two.
